title: Erroll Garner and Art Tatum on opposite ends of 52nd Street
summary: Jones recalls his first night in New York looking from Garner to Tatum like watching a tennis match.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How long did you know Erroll Garner?
Since about 1944, when I first went to New York.

That's when I first met him. He was working on 52nd Street, too. He was working towards the end of the block, and there was so much excitement. There was Erroll Garner on one end of the block and Art Tatum on the other end. And gee whiz, I didn't know which way to turn my head. I was like looking at a tennis match.

So John Levy and I laugh about that today. Our first day in New York. We could only -- we only stayed up till about 12:00 o'clock, because we were so high, we were going from one bar to the other, and got so excited and looking at Art and Dizzy and all these guys at clubs, back to back, you know?

That's the way the street was laid out. And to see everybody within one block. And we just -- you know, in Chicago or something like Los Angeles, it's kind of spread out. But we -- and then to be able to talk with them, and hang out with them, on intermissions and everything, you know? So --
